notes.meaning: The parents confirmed that the man was their son and that he was born blind, but they refused to say how he was cured or who did it. Since he was an adult under Jewish law, he was legally old enough to speak on his own behalf. They passed the questioning to him so they would not get into trouble.

The parents dodged the questions because the religious leaders had agreed to throw out anyone who accepted Jesus as the Christ, the promised Savior. Being put out of the synagogue meant being cut off from worship, family, and community life. Out of fear, the parents left their son to stand before the judges on his own.

The leaders called the healed man back and ordered him to give glory to God, a formal phrase used when putting someone under oath to confess the truth. They insisted that Jesus was a lawbreaker and demanded that the man agree with their verdict. They hoped to bully him into denying the miracle.

The man refused to debate whether Jesus was a sinner and focused entirely on what had happened to him. He boldly declared that while he might not know all the answers, he was certain that he had been blind and could now see. His simple, firsthand experience was proof that the leaders could not disprove.

The rulers asked him again to explain what Jesus did and how He had cured his eyes. They repeated the question hoping the man would change his story or give them an excuse to accuse Jesus of doing wrong. His clear testimony had trapped them, and they were looking for any way out.

The man bluntly answered that he had already told them the story and they had refused to pay attention. He then asked with biting humor if they wanted to hear it again because they were planning to become Jesus' disciples. His fearless words showed that he saw right through their bad motives.

Furious at his sarcastic reply, the leaders insulted him and shouted that he was a follower of Jesus. They proudly claimed to be disciples of Moses, the great lawgiver of Israel. In their minds, following Jesus meant turning away from the law God gave to Moses.

The leaders argued that God had clearly spoken to Moses and proven his authority, but they claimed to know nothing about where Jesus came from. They used their respect for the past as an excuse to reject God's present messenger. Pride made them reject the very prophet Moses wrote about.

The healed man expressed amazement that the nation's top teachers could not tell where Jesus came from. He pointed out the obvious contradiction: these experts claimed ignorance, yet Jesus had just performed an astounding miracle on his eyes. A genuine miracle was clear proof of God's power at work.

The man reminded the leaders of a truth everyone knew: God does not grant miraculous answers to ungodly impostors, but hears those who revere Him and obey His will. Since God had clearly answered Jesus by working this miracle, Jesus could not be an evil sinner. Genuine obedience to God leads to real spiritual power.

differ.view: Some evangelicals explain that the man was merely repeating common Jewish thought, not stating divine doctrine, because God graciously hears any sinner who calls out for salvation.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic commentary notes that God does not answer unrepentant sinners by granting them the power to work miracles in support of their teaching.

notes.meaning: The man emphasized that since the beginning of time, no one had ever heard of a person born blind receiving sight. Not even the great Old Testament prophets had ever performed such a sign. This unprecedented miracle showed that God was working through Jesus in a brand-new way.

The man concluded with simple logic: if Jesus were not from God, He could never have done such a miracle. His reasoning completely destroyed the Pharisees' claim that Jesus was an ungodly lawbreaker. When God backs someone with divine power, the evidence cannot be denied.

Unable to answer his logic, the leaders angrily insulted the man, claiming his blindness at birth proved he was totally sinful. They rejected the idea that an uneducated beggar could teach them, and they threw him out of the synagogue. When proud people lose an argument, they often turn to anger and punishment.

When Jesus heard that the rulers had cast the man out, He went looking for him and found him. Jesus asked him if he believed in the Son of Man, a title for the Messiah, God's chosen King. Jesus cares deeply for those who are rejected for standing up for the truth.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Modern scholars note that the earliest Greek manuscripts read 'Son of Man' instead of 'Son of God', though both titles identify Jesus as the Messiah.

notes.meaning: The man asked who the Son of Man was so that he could place his trust in Him. Because he had been blind when Jesus first touched him, he had never actually seen his healer's face. His humble question showed that he was ready to believe whatever Jesus taught him.

Jesus revealed Himself plainly, telling the man that he was looking right at the Messiah and hearing His voice. Just as He had done with the woman at the well, Jesus spoke clearly about His identity to someone others looked down on. This personal revelation completed the miracle of giving him physical sight.

The man immediately believed and fell down to worship Jesus. In Jewish life, worship was reserved for God alone, so by accepting this worship, Jesus revealed that He is truly God. Believing in Jesus naturally leads to praising and honoring Him.

Jesus announced that He came into the world for judgment, meaning His presence acts like a sifter that reveals who people really are. Those who admit their spiritual blindness receive sight, while those who boast that they already see are left in darkness. Coming to Jesus begins by admitting our need for Him.

Some Pharisees nearby heard Jesus say this and realized His words were aimed at them. Insulted that anyone would think they were in the dark, they asked indignantly if He was calling them blind too. Their proud question showed that they were completely blind to their own spiritual state.

Jesus answered that if they were truly unaware of the truth, they would not be held guilty. But because they claimed to have perfect spiritual sight while deliberately rejecting God's Son, their guilt remained. Pretending to be righteous only keeps a person trapped in sin.
